_meta.note: Plain-language explanations written for this project from general medical knowledge. Each entry points to a reputable public source for further reading. Only the CBC and hemoglobin links go to a specific page; the others point to the MedlinePlus lab tests index. Have a qualified professional review before relying on them.

hemoglobin.measures: Hemoglobin is the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen around the body.
hemoglobin.high: A high level can be linked to long-term low oxygen levels, living at high altitude, or too many red blood cells. A doctor needs to look at the cause.
hemoglobin.low: A low level can be linked to anemia, blood loss, low iron or other vitamin levels, or other conditions. A doctor needs to look at the cause.
hemoglobin.source: MedlinePlus Lab Tests (NIH, U.S. National Library of Medicine)

wbc.measures: White blood cells are part of the immune system and help the body fight infection.
wbc.high: A high count can be seen with infections, inflammation, stress, some medicines and other conditions.
wbc.low: A low count can be seen with some infections, medicines, immune or bone marrow conditions.
wbc.source: MedlinePlus Lab Tests (NIH, U.S. National Library of Medicine)

platelets.measures: Platelets are small cell pieces that help blood to clot and stop bleeding.
platelets.high: A high count can be seen with inflammation, iron deficiency and some blood conditions.
platelets.low: A low count can raise the chance of bleeding or bruising and has many possible causes, so it should be checked by a doctor.
platelets.source: MedlinePlus Lab Tests (NIH, U.S. National Library of Medicine)

rbc.measures: Red blood cells carry oxygen. The RBC count is the number of red blood cells in a small amount of blood.
rbc.high: A high count can be linked to dehydration, low oxygen levels or other conditions.
rbc.low: A low count can be linked to anemia, blood loss or other conditions.
rbc.source: MedlinePlus Lab Tests (NIH, U.S. National Library of Medicine)

glucose_fasting.measures: Fasting blood sugar is the sugar (glucose) level in blood after not eating for at least 8 hours.
glucose_fasting.high: A high fasting level can be a sign of problems with blood sugar control. One result alone is not a diagnosis, and doctors usually repeat or confirm it.
glucose_fasting.low: A low level can cause shakiness, sweating or weakness and can be linked to medicines, long gaps without food or other conditions.
glucose_fasting.source: MedlinePlus Lab Tests (NIH, U.S. National Library of Medicine)

hba1c.measures: HbA1c shows the average blood sugar level over about the last 2 to 3 months.
hba1c.high: A high value means blood sugar has been higher than the usual target. A doctor uses it with other tests to decide what it means.
hba1c.low: A low value is uncommon and may be related to some blood conditions or medicines.
hba1c.source: MedlinePlus Lab Tests (NIH, U.S. National Library of Medicine)

cholesterol_total.measures: Total cholesterol is the overall amount of cholesterol, a fat-like substance, in the blood.
cholesterol_total.high: A high level is linked to a higher chance of heart and blood vessel disease over time. A doctor looks at the full lipid panel and other risk factors.
cholesterol_total.low: A very low level is uncommon and can have different causes, so it is worth mentioning to a doctor.
cholesterol_total.source: MedlinePlus Lab Tests (NIH, U.S. National Library of Medicine)

ldl.measures: LDL is often called 'bad' cholesterol because high levels can build up in blood vessel walls.
ldl.high: A high level is linked to a higher chance of heart and blood vessel disease over time.
ldl.low: A low level is usually not a concern on its own.
ldl.source: MedlinePlus Lab Tests (NIH, U.S. National Library of Medicine)

hdl.measures: HDL is often called 'good' cholesterol because it helps remove other cholesterol from the blood.
hdl.high: A high level is usually not a concern.
hdl.low: A low level is linked to a higher chance of heart and blood vessel disease over time.
hdl.source: MedlinePlus Lab Tests (NIH, U.S. National Library of Medicine)

triglycerides.measures: Triglycerides are a type of fat in the blood. Levels rise after meals and with some medical conditions.
triglycerides.high: A high level is linked to a higher chance of heart disease, and very high levels can affect the pancreas. A doctor looks at the full picture.
triglycerides.low: A low level is usually not a concern.
triglycerides.source: MedlinePlus Lab Tests (NIH, U.S. National Library of Medicine)

creatinine.measures: Creatinine is a waste product from muscles that the kidneys remove. It helps show how well the kidneys filter blood.
creatinine.high: A high level can mean the kidneys are not filtering as well as usual, or can be linked to dehydration, muscle mass or medicines. A doctor needs to check.
creatinine.low: A low level is often related to low muscle mass and is usually not a concern on its own.
creatinine.source: MedlinePlus Lab Tests (NIH, U.S. National Library of Medicine)

uric_acid.measures: Uric acid is a waste product made when the body breaks down certain foods and cells.
uric_acid.high: A high level can be linked to gout or kidney stones in some people, and also to diet, medicines and kidney function.
uric_acid.low: A low level is uncommon and usually not a concern on its own.
uric_acid.source: MedlinePlus Lab Tests (NIH, U.S. National Library of Medicine)

alt.measures: ALT is an enzyme found mostly in the liver. It can leak into the blood when liver cells are irritated or damaged.
alt.high: A high level can be linked to liver irritation from many causes such as medicines, alcohol, fatty liver or infections. A doctor needs to look at the cause.
alt.low: A low level is usually not a concern.
alt.source: MedlinePlus Lab Tests (NIH, U.S. National Library of Medicine)

ast.measures: AST is an enzyme found in the liver and also in muscles and other organs.
ast.high: A high level can be linked to liver irritation, muscle injury or other causes. A doctor usually reads it together with ALT.
ast.low: A low level is usually not a concern.
ast.source: MedlinePlus Lab Tests (NIH, U.S. National Library of Medicine)

alp.measures: ALP is an enzyme found in the liver, bile ducts and bones.
alp.high: A high level can be linked to liver or bile duct problems or to bone conditions. A doctor needs to look at the cause.
alp.low: A low level is uncommon and can have different causes.
alp.source: MedlinePlus Lab Tests (NIH, U.S. National Library of Medicine)

bilirubin_total.measures: Bilirubin is a yellow substance made when old red blood cells are broken down. The liver removes it from the body.
bilirubin_total.high: A high level can cause yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice) and can be linked to liver, bile duct or blood conditions.
bilirubin_total.low: A low level is usually not a concern.
bilirubin_total.source: MedlinePlus Lab Tests (NIH, U.S. National Library of Medicine)

albumin.measures: Albumin is a protein made by the liver. It keeps fluid in the blood vessels and carries substances around the body.
albumin.high: A high level is often related to dehydration.
albumin.low: A low level can be linked to liver or kidney conditions, poor nutrition or long-term illness.
albumin.source: MedlinePlus Lab Tests (NIH, U.S. National Library of Medicine)

tsh.measures: TSH is a hormone from the pituitary gland that tells the thyroid how much thyroid hormone to make.
tsh.high: A high TSH can be linked to an underactive thyroid. A doctor usually checks it together with thyroid hormone levels.
tsh.low: A low TSH can be linked to an overactive thyroid or some medicines. A doctor usually checks it together with thyroid hormone levels.
tsh.source: MedlinePlus Lab Tests (NIH, U.S. National Library of Medicine)

potassium.measures: Potassium is a mineral that helps nerves, muscles and the heart work normally.
potassium.high: A high level can affect the heart rhythm and needs prompt medical advice, especially if it is far above the range.
potassium.low: A low level can cause weakness or muscle cramps and can affect the heart rhythm, so it needs medical advice.
potassium.source: MedlinePlus Lab Tests (NIH, U.S. National Library of Medicine)

sodium.measures: Sodium is a mineral that helps control body water and blood pressure.
sodium.high: A high level is often linked to not enough water in the body.
sodium.low: A low level can be linked to too much water, some medicines or medical conditions and can cause confusion or weakness if it is far below the range.
sodium.source: MedlinePlus Lab Tests (NIH, U.S. National Library of Medicine)

vitamin_d.measures: Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium and keeps bones and muscles healthy.
vitamin_d.high: A very high level is uncommon and is usually related to taking too many supplements.
vitamin_d.low: A low level is common and can be linked to little sun exposure, diet or some conditions. A doctor may suggest food, sunlight or supplements.
vitamin_d.source: MedlinePlus Lab Tests (NIH, U.S. National Library of Medicine)

ferritin.measures: Ferritin is a protein that stores iron. The level shows how much iron the body has stored.
ferritin.high: A high level can be linked to inflammation, liver conditions or too much iron.
ferritin.low: A low level is a common sign of low iron stores.
ferritin.source: MedlinePlus Lab Tests (NIH, U.S. National Library of Medicine)
